derivation.policy: Project only exact tuples present in both original device manifests and original framework matrices. All source declarations use exact instances. AIDL omitted version is recorded separately and projected as explicit version 1.

limitations: This device-specific compatibility declaration does not implement or enable a service. The preserved proprietary binaries and their framework clients require independent runtime and ABI validation.

android.se.omapi is the exact original vendor VINTF declaration, with an existing frozen AOSP version1 interface. The pinned SecureElement app conditionally registers ISecureElementService/default for the system user when secure_element_vintf_enabled is true. This is distinct from android.hardware.secure_element; selected resources, app inclusion and runtime registration remain unverified.
com.android.ozoaudio.notify, com.fingerprints.fpc.extension and vendor.dolby declarations are retained as original proprietary interfaces, despite their different package prefixes.

Three original product-matrix tuples are deliberately projected into the single Nezha system device FCM. This consolidates static framework support declarations only and does not move any runtime service or proprietary file.
The original stock device matrix has additional legacy declarations and version ranges, which are not imported. Duplicate original entries are coalesced and retained as provenance.
Private original XML and receipts are reopened for generation, not copied into the portable candidate. Source image hashes remain provenance; this helper does not reread complete original images.
The pinned checker does not compare HAL presence in HalManifest::checkCompatibility. This extension addresses its observed checkUnusedHals error and is not a complete service implementation test.
required_native_checks: Verify source pins and every source_preconditions identity in the existing checkout; preserve all reviewed patches, original proprietary inputs and previous failed native evidence.

Install a separately recorded device candidate. The changed source files are generated/BoardConfigCandidate.mk and the new generated/framework-compatibility-matrix.xml; the product fragment, SELinux inputs and provider binaries must remain unchanged.

Run normal framework_compatibility_matrix.device.xml and check-vintf-all component goals. Confirm exported DeviceFrameworkCompatibilityMatrixFile is the exact singleton source path, no product selector is active, and the native Ninja producer consumes that path. Inspect the installed matrix rather than assuming source/output byte equality.

Verify the installed device FCM contains exactly these 155 AIDL tuples without regex or version ranges, while retaining the normal generated SELinux and AVB requirements. Preserve all numbered platform FCM identities.

Recapture the selected framework/vendor/ODM/kernel/APEX inputs after the matrix build; run all original framework consistency, vendor/ODM consistency and full --check-compat commands, with all 39 selected APEX packages materialized and the stock kernel configuration supplied.

Retain the pinned no-level matrix-definition skip and other native validator coverage limits explicitly. Offline XML projection and a native unused-HAL pass do not prove interface implementations, runtime service registration, full ABI, encryption, OTA or boot.
